evidence.reference_title: ARF1-related disorder: phenotypic and molecular spectrum.
evidence.snippet: We confirm the role of ARF1 in an autosomal dominant syndrome with a phenotypic spectrum including severe ID, microcephaly, seizures and PVNH due to impaired neuronal migration.

nodes.description: ARF1 is a small GTPase that acts as a molecular switch at the Golgi, inactive when bound to GDP and active when bound to GTP. Heterozygous disease variants disrupt this cycle, but the direction of the functional effect is contested: for the same recurrent p.R99H variant one study found a decreased level of steady-state active (GTP-bound) ARF1, while others found increased GDP/GTP exchange and constitutive activation. The readings converge on Golgi disruption regardless (see the mechanism controversy in discussions).

evidence.reference_title: Variations associated with neurodevelopmental disorders affect ARF1 function and cortical development.
evidence.snippet: ARF1-p.R19C, -p.F51L, -p.R99C and -p.R99H exhibit higher GDP/GTP exchange activity compared to ARF1 wild type (WT).

nodes.description: Dysregulated ARF1 disrupts COPI-dependent vesicular transport at the Golgi apparatus. Expression of disease variants causes swelling and expansion of the Golgi in cultured cells and in migrating cortical neurons.

evidence.reference_title: A neurodevelopmental disorder associated with an activating de novo missense variant in ARF1.
evidence.snippet: the expression of this variant caused swelling of the Golgi apparatus

evidence.reference_title: Variations associated with neurodevelopmental disorders affect ARF1 function and cortical development.
evidence.snippet: Expression of these variants resulted in the expansion of the Golgi apparatus in migrating cortical neurons.

nodes.description: Neurons fail to initiate migration from the periventricular germinal zone to the cortical plate, arresting as nodules along the lateral ventricle walls.

evidence.reference_title: Variations associated with neurodevelopmental disorders affect ARF1 function and cortical development.
evidence.snippet: In utero electroporation-mediated gene transfer into the cortical neurons of embryonic mice demonstrated that p.R99C, p.R99H and p.K127E cause a migration defect.

evidence.reference_title: Filamin A regulates neuronal migration through brefeldin A-inhibited guanine exchange factor 2-dependent Arf1 activation.
evidence.snippet: Loss of Arf1 activity disrupts neuronal migration and cell adhesion.

nodes.description: Nodules of gray matter lining the walls of the lateral ventricles, the MONDO-defining feature; present in a minority of the reported cohort.

evidence.reference_title: ARF1-related disorder: phenotypic and molecular spectrum.
evidence.snippet: Microcephaly below 3 SD was noted in 10 individuals (50%; 10/20), seizures of various types were reported in 8 (50%; 8/16) and PVNH in 3 (20%, 3/15).

evidence.reference_title: ARF1-related disorder: phenotypic and molecular spectrum.
evidence.snippet: neuronal migration defects including PVNH, cortical dysplasia, polymicrogyria (45%; 9/20) and corpus callosum abnormalities (50%; 10/20)

nodes.description: Impaired vesicle trafficking and cell-cell adhesion compromise the apical attachment of radial glial cells and the integrity of the neuroependymal lining at the ventricular surface, the scaffold on which neurons migrate.

evidence.reference_title: ARF1 haploinsufficiency causes periventricular nodular heterotopia with variable clinical expressivity.
evidence.snippet: The primary anatomical defect leading to periventricular nodular heterotopia occurs within the neural progenitors along the neuroepithelial lining of the lateral ventricles and results from a defect in the initiation of neuronal migration, following disruption of the neuroependyma and impaired neuronal motility.

evidence.reference_title: Filamin A regulates neuronal migration through brefeldin A-inhibited guanine exchange factor 2-dependent Arf1 activation.
evidence.snippet: coordinated interactions between actin (through FlnA) and vesicle trafficking (through Big2-Arf) direct the assembly and disassembly of membrane protein complexes required for neuronal migration and neuroependymal integrity.

nodes.description: Recurrent de novo missense variant (c.296G>A; p.R99H) identified in multiple unrelated individuals, and the variant carrying the most functional data. Those data conflict: some studies report increased GDP/GTP exchange, tighter binding to the effector GGA3 and constitutive activation, while another reports a decreased level of steady-state active ARF1 (the mechanism controversy recorded in discussions). They agree it disrupts the Golgi and causes a neuronal migration defect; notably one R99H individual did not have periventricular nodular heterotopia.

evidence.reference_title: A neurodevelopmental disorder associated with an activating de novo missense variant in ARF1.
evidence.snippet: we report a pediatric patient with an ARF1-related disorder because of a monoallelic de novo missense variant (c.296 G > A; p.R99H) in the ARF1 gene, associated with developmental delay, hypotonia, intellectual disability and motor stereotypies.

evidence.reference_title: A neurodevelopmental disorder associated with an activating de novo missense variant in ARF1.
evidence.snippet: The absence of periventricular nodular heterotopias in this R99H-ARF1 subject also indicates that this finding may not be a consistent phenotypic expression of all ARF1-related disorders.

nodes.description: De novo missense variant (c.509T>C; p.Leu170Pro) reported in the first Chinese individual with ARF1-related disease, who presented with drug-refractory focal epilepsy and mild developmental delay but no periventricular nodular heterotopia. Molecular modelling and co-immunoprecipitation indicate it weakens the ARF1-GGA3 effector interaction, reinforcing that PVNH is not an obligate feature.
